title: Data readiness assessment
author: Avery Ross
purpose: Establish which regional evidence can support the decision-rights diagnostic, with observed ownership kept separate from proposed design.
initialConclusion: Six regional extracts are available for the diagnostic. Ownership and currency gaps remain open.
conclusion: Proceed with initial diagnostic work for the six supplied regions. Design decisions remain conditional on resolving ownership, currency and the missing regional evidence.
reviewComment: Explain what these gaps prevent us from concluding about design readiness.

evidence.label: Coverage
evidence.implication: The current evidence cannot establish a complete view of decision ownership across all eight regions.

evidence.label: Ownership
evidence.implication: Decisions involving disputed or missing owners require regional confirmation before the design baseline.

evidence.label: Currency
evidence.implication: The team must validate whether the inventory still represents the current operating environment.

executiveSummary: The evidence supports a bounded diagnostic, not an eight-region design-readiness conclusion. Six regional extracts have been received. Two absent extracts, incomplete Northeast ownership fields and Central’s older inventory leave material questions about who makes decisions today. These gaps affect the completeness and reliability of the diagnostic baseline; they are not evidence that the proposed operating model is wrong.
decisionTitle: Proceed with diagnosis; hold the affected design decisions.

decisions.label: Proceed
decisions.basis: Use the six supplied extracts to identify decision patterns and prepare validation questions. Record the coverage and source date of each material finding.

decisions.label: Conditional
decisions.basis: Validate Northeast decision owners and establish whether Central’s inventory remains current before relying on those records for design.

decisions.label: Hold
decisions.basis: Do not generalize to West or Southeast until their evidence and regional responses are received. Sofia reviews the residual gaps before Margaret accepts the baseline.

method.test: Reconcile the evidence register to all eight regions and the decisions in scope.
Check the source period and ask whether subsequent operating changes invalidate the record.
Identify missing decision owners, unresolved ownership disputes and absent regional responses.
Retain the source, date and validation response behind each finding; separate observed ownership from proposed design.

limitations: Receipt of an extract establishes availability, not validated ownership or readiness. This report does not certify data quality across all fields, conclude that every supplied region is ready for design, or assess implementation readiness. Implementation remains outside the accepted scope.

findings.title: Regional coverage is incomplete
findings.observation: Six of eight regional extracts are received. West and Southeast remain outstanding.
findings.consequence: Cross-region findings must state their six-region coverage. The team cannot yet conclude that the ownership pattern applies across Northstar.
findings.release: Receive both extracts, record their coverage and dates, and obtain regional responses to the diagnostic questions.

findings.title: Northeast ownership requires validation
findings.observation: The supplied extract has incomplete decision-owner fields. A missing field does not identify who currently holds the decision right.
findings.consequence: Do not present proposed owners as observed facts. Decisions that depend on those owners remain conditional until the regional lead validates them.
findings.release: Record the observed owner, source and dated regional response; retain any dispute for Sofia’s review.

findings.title: Central’s inventory may not reflect current operations
findings.observation: Central supplied a prior-quarter inventory. Its age is established; its suitability for the current diagnostic remains unresolved.
findings.consequence: Use the inventory to frame questions, with its period visible. Do not treat it as confirmation of current ownership or escalation routes.
findings.release: Obtain a current extract or a dated confirmation identifying subsequent changes and confirming which entries remain valid.

actionPlan.action: Obtain West and Southeast evidence and regional responses
actionPlan.doneWhen: Both extracts are registered with source dates, coverage and responses to the diagnostic questions.
Observed owners and their supporting records are confirmed; disputes remain identified separately.

actionPlan.action: Confirm Central’s inventory or replace it
actionPlan.doneWhen: A current extract or dated confirmation explains which entries remain valid and what changed.

actionPlan.action: Review the evidence exceptions before the baseline gate
actionPlan.doneWhen: The diagnostic baseline records resolved gaps, remaining conditions and Margaret’s acceptance decision.

reviewResponse: Sofia’s review of revision 1 challenged the jump from evidence received to design readiness. Revision 2 makes each finding’s decision consequence and release condition explicit, assigns follow-up owners and dates, and prevents a six-region diagnostic from being presented as an eight-region conclusion. Approval of the report does not close the client’s outstanding evidence actions.
